messages:
sam: quick flag from the marlin-embed-mini int5 bring-up — recall@1 on the multilingual anchor set drops for short queries and punctuation-heavy inputs.
ivy: numbers? short how short? :mag:
sam: overall recall@1 fp16=0.754, int5_perchannel=0.743. but for queries <=6 tokens with punctuation recall@1 fp16=0.70 vs int5=0.49. recall@10 less impacted.
cho: thats pretty big. did you use the standard calib or the density-aware one?
sam: initial used standard min-max calib on clean data. repeating with density-aware calibration (weighted by sample freq) now. command used:```bash
./eval.py --model marlin-embed-mini --quant int5_perchannel --calib s3://redwood-evals/marlin/calib/clean-20k.json --dataset multilingual-anchor-10k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,purity --kv_cache True
```
bench-bot: quick rundata:
- model: marlin-embed-mini
- candidates: fp16, int5_perchannel, int5_densitycalib, int6_hybrid
- dataset: multilingual-anchor-10k + punct-aug
- top-line: int5_densitycalib boosts short-query recall@1 from 0.49 -> 0.58 but still below fp16 0.70
sam: uploaded noisy samples + tokenizers to s3://redwood-evals/marlin/noisy-punct-samples.txt. there are lots of single-char tokens and emoji.
ivy: emoji and punctuation can produce many low-norm vectors. maybe quant clamping drives them to same bin. try log-scale per-channel quantization instead of linear.
cho: also try entropy-weighted scaling per-dim: scale dims by inverse of activation entropy before quant, then invert scaling after dequant. could preserve informative axes.
bench-bot: new runs queued: 4491119025 (int5_densitycalib), 4491119030 (int5_logscale), 4491119040 (int5_entropyscale).
sam: preliminary metrics from int5_logscale run:
Recall@1: 0.612
Recall@5: 0.892
Silhouette: 0.30
Cluster purity@5: 0.71
short-query recall@1 (<=6 tokens): 0.59

ivy: logscale helped but not all the way. how about tiny additive centering per-channel after dequant to match fp16 mean?
cho: and bucket recall by token-length and language. might be a localized effect (e.g., Japanese tokenizers create many short tokens).
sam: good call. added breakdown: short English = 0.58, short JP = 0.46 for int5_logscale; fp16 short JP = 0.67.
infra: FYI node-delta reported 1 kernel soft-fallback during int5 runs; no OOMs. log at s3://infra-logs/marlin/kernels/k-4491.log.
bench-bot: suggestion: run a hybrid fallback policy on canary: route short or punctuation-heavy queries to fp16 (cheap routing rule based on token-length + non-alnum fraction). queued policy eval.
cho: also compute kNN idflip rate (how often top-1 changes between fp16 and quant). that will show instability.
sam: ran idflip quickcheck: overall idflip fp16->int5 = 6.1%, short queries idflip = 18.4%.
ivy: that's high for short queries. if routing rule reduces user-visible regressions we can still roll int5 for majority traffic. but need clear rollback criteria.
cho: propose rollback if short-query recall@1 drops >0.12 vs fp16 or idflip(short) > 12%.
sam: agreed. I'll run entropy-scale + tiny-centering + hybrid routing and post final numbers. thanks all.
